walkthroughs.body_html:
Life in the Universe — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Life in the Universe brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Life in the Universe.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Radius of the observable universe in Gly?

options: WWW
Filaments and voids
CMB pattern
Solar wind
Infinite.
Galaxies only move in random directions.
All galaxies move at the same speed.
More distant galaxies recede faster - their recession velocity is proportional to distance.

mcqs.q: What is the current best estimate for the age of the universe?
options: Infinite.
About 6,000 years.
About 13.8 billion years.
Whether it has planets.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a star becomes a white dwarf or a neutron star?
options: Its colour during its main sequence phase.
Whether it has planets.
Infinite.
Its mass - low/medium mass becomes a white dwarf; massive stars produce neutron stars or black holes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Critical density”?
options: Density at which the universe is geometrically flat; ~9 x 10^-27 kg/m^3.
Speculative ideas of multiple disconnected universes; outside present observational reach.
Boundary beyond which the universe is unobservable due to finite light travel time.
Network of filaments and voids forming the 'cosmic web' on >100 Mpc scales.
